conventions: bpp = Mbps*1e6/(W*H*fps) of the recorded file resolution; fixed = codecs whose bitrate does not scale with resolution/fps choice

cameras.name: iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max
cameras.notes: Apple tech specs (support 111829, 15 Pro; 15 Pro Max identical video specs): 4K at 24/25/30/60 fps; 1080p at 25/30/60; 720p30; slo-mo 1080p 120/240; Cinematic up to 4K HDR 30; Action mode up to 2.8K 60 (pixel size not published, omitted); spatial 1080p30; Dolby Vision HDR up to 4K60. 'ProRes video recording up to 4K at 60 fps with external recording.' Formats: HEVC, H.264, ProRes. Log video recording (Apple Log, a transfer curve - does not change ProRes data rates) and ACES. No ProRes RAW listed in tech specs. Support 109041: 4K60 ProRes requires external USB-C drive >=220 MB/s (exFAT, USB 3 10 Gb/s cable); no 4K120 on 15 Pro; built-in ProRes supports HDR, SDR and Log.

codecs.name: ProRes 422 HQ
codecs.ref: Apple ProRes White Paper (April 2022), target data rate ProRes 422 HQ 1920x1080 29.97p = 220 Mb/s (bpp = Mbps*1e6/(1920*1080*29.97)). Native Camera app records ProRes 422 HQ (flavor not named on apple.com; consistent with Apple's 220 MB/s external-drive requirement for 4K60 = ~1768 Mb/s 422 HQ). iPhone ProRes limits (Apple support 109041): built-in storage 4K at 24/25/30 fps (256 GB+), 1080p 25/30 (128 GB) or 25/30/60 (256 GB+); 4K60 requires an external drive >=220 MB/s; 4K120 not available on 15 Pro. ProRes not available in Cinematic, slo-mo or time-lapse.

codecs.name: ProRes 422
codecs.ref: Apple ProRes White Paper (April 2022), target data rate ProRes 422 1920x1080 29.97p = 147 Mb/s (bpp = Mbps*1e6/(1920*1080*29.97)). Only via third-party apps (e.g. Blackmagic Camera); not the native Camera app - third-party info.
